page.layout: One page of text, single column; running head at top; page number at top left; no notes beside the text block; a few stray marks only.

main_text.p: nis authoritatem, alia multa suadent. Gethicam autem non aliam quàm Gothicam, sive Germanicam fuisse, suo loco probabimus.

- Τυλὸς, vel ut alii, γνώΘ, pera militaris, in quâ viaticum, & alia necessaria milites circumferebant. Hinc videtur Anglicum to gull, defraudare, fluxisse; quo modo & Latinum, manticulari, pro furari, dolosè agere, ex simili ratione. Affinis vox, to begutle, ex gutle, (quod & togle; de quo suprà;, fraus, impostura :) ad quam si priorem illam malit aliquis referre, fruatur suo judicio; ego aliter censeo.

Τωειὰω, subsanno; falsè rideo. Ita vulgò ex Plutarcho in Lycurgo docent. Ibi certè in ῥῆτρα quadam Lycurgi vetere, extremâ, reperio: ἔτως εἰσφέρειν τε ᾧ ἀρ- ισαδς γαμωλᾶν γεσὰν ἢ μὴ ᾧ κεχτ; ut praestantissima Henrici Stephani editio illa exhibet. Quae miror à Plutarcho, qui cetera istius Sciti explicat, praeterita esse. Si is est locus quem volunt, infirmo fundamento nititur ista expositio. Sed de verbo Graeco aliàs fortasse quaeremus, cùm aliae erunt Plutarchi.

page.notes: Greek words are partly doubtful and marked only in the text where unclear; the Greek lines in the middle of the page are approximate. Catchword "tarchi" at lower right is taken as the line end of "Plutarchi" and not as a catchword. The mark "{ }" under "Plu-" and small marks at the foot are stains, not text.
